"Let $q$ be a prime power, let $4\leq\ell<t$ be integers, and let $\operatorname{NG}(q,t)$ denote the projective norm graph. A set of vertices has common neighbours if those vertices are all adjacent to each such common vertex.

**Higher-wise independence conjecture.** For any prime power $q$ and integers $4\leq\ell<t$, all but $o(n^\ell)$ sets of $\ell$ vertices in $\operatorname{NG}(q,t)$ have $(1+o(1))q^{t-\ell}$ common neighbours.

The claim extends the established asymptotic description of common neighbourhoods from triples to larger sets of vertices. The paper presents it as being supported by computer calculations; its general validity remains open."
statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $4\leq\ell<t$ be integers, and let $\operatorname{NG}(q,t)$ denote the projective norm graph. A set of vertices has common neighbours if those vertices are all adjacent to each such common vertex.

**Higher-wise independence conjecture.** For any prime power $q$ and integers $4\leq\ell<t$, all but $o(n^\ell)$ sets of $\ell$ vertices in $\operatorname{NG}(q,t)$ have $(1+o(1))q^{t-\ell}$ common neighbours.

The claim extends the established asymptotic description of common neighbourhoods from triples to larger sets of vertices. The paper presents it as being supported by computer calculations; its general validity remains open.

**Koolen's conjecture.** For almost all finite connected simple graphs, the Terwilliger algebras coincide with the full matrix algebras.

Is there a graph $G$ with vertex set $\omega_2^2$ and chromatic number $\aleph_2$ such that every subgraph whose vertices have a lesser type has chromatic number $\leq \aleph_0$?
What if instead we ask for $G$ to have chromatic number $\aleph_1$?
